body.text: You need an item's number, two columns at once, a table of lists and a copy you can edit safely.

slides.title: Iteration with numbers
slides.sub: enumerate yields pairs: index and item
slides.main: One loop header instead of a counter, len and indexing.

body.text: ON SCREEN

1 Anya
2 Boris
3 Vera
Without start, counting begins at 0; start=1 gives normal numbering from one.

slides.title: Two lists at once
slides.sub: zip closes lists tooth by tooth
slides.main: zip stops at the shortest list: the tail is silently lost.

body.text:
names = ["Anya", "Boris"]
scores = [5, 4]
for name, score in zip(names, scores):
    print(name, score)
ON SCREEN

Anya 5
Boris 4
Works for three lists or more: just list them with commas.

slides.main: Empty result, loop, condition, append: the source stays untouched.

slides.title: Nested lists
slides.sub: A list of rows, each row a list too
slides.main: A table cell takes two indexes in a row: row, then column.

body.text:
grid = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]
print(grid[1][2])    # 6
grid[0][0] = 99
for row in grid:
    print(row)
ON SCREEN
Walk a table with two nested loops: outer over rows, inner over items.

slides.title: References
slides.sub: b = a hangs a second name tag on the list
slides.main: The list is a house, the name an address: copy the envelope, one house.

body.text:
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)    # [1, 2, 3, 4] — the same list!

slides.title: A real copy
slides.sub: Slice, copy method or list function
slides.main: The copy is shallow: nested lists stay shared.

body.text:
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a.copy()      # or a[:] or list(a)
b.append(4)
print(a, b)       # [1, 2, 3] [1, 2, 3, 4]

cells.sub: Table rows are still shared: use a deep copy

slides.title: Equality and identity
slides.main: For "is the data the same", always use ==.

body.text:
a = [1, 2]
b = a.copy()
c = a
print(a == b)    # True  — same contents
print(a is b)    # False — different objects
print(a is c)    # True  — the very same one
Order matters: the same numbers in another order are unequal lists.

slides.title: Don't edit a list in a loop
slides.sub: Deleting shifts items, the loop skips one
slides.main: Build a new list or loop over a copy: for x in nums[:].

slides.title: More methods
slides.sub: index, count, reversing, slices with summaries
slides.main: Behind every one-liner there is a loop, just hidden inside.

body.text:
nums = [5, 3, 5, 1]
print(nums.index(3))    # 1 — position of first match
print(nums.count(5))    # 2 — how many times
print(nums[::-1])       # [1, 5, 3, 5] — reversed copy
print(max(nums[:2]))    # 5 — max of the first two
No such item: index fails. Check with in first.

slides.title: Typical traps
slides.sub: append returns nothing; multiplying copies a reference
slides.main: Build table rows with a loop: a fresh list each pass.

body.text:
nums = [3, 1]
nums = nums.append(5)
print(nums)            # None — the list is wiped out!

grid = [[0] * 3] * 3   # three references to one row
grid[0][0] = 7
print(grid)            # [[7, 0, 0], [7, 0, 0], [7, 0, 0]]
Also: an empty list breaks nums[0] and nums.pop(); check the length first.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Don't delete items from a list you are looping over.
